correctness.rationale: Let a=d−1≥2. In characteristic p, a=−1, so Y_i∂_iF=t_{i−1}−t_i for t_i=c_iY_i^aY_{i+1}. At a projective singular point all t_i=t, and F=mt=0 with p∤m gives t=0. With all c_i nonzero some Y_j must vanish; ∂_jF then forces its predecessor to vanish and iteration contradicts projectivity. If c_i=0, e_i is singular, even at further coefficient degenerations. Hence the reduced discriminant splits as the coordinate hyperplanes, geometrically SNC; exponent one in the reduced norm product and one transitive Frobenius orbit give irreducibility over the base. Frobenius conjugates c_i=z^{q^i} produce the norm. Over Q=q^s the descended algebra splits into g=gcd(m,s) factors of size Q^ℓ for ℓ=m/g. Exactly k nonzero factors give binomial(g,k)(Q^ℓ−1)^k vectors with free scalar division by Q−1. All factors must be nonzero for smoothness; g=1 is exactly the all-smooth case and the least g>1 occurs at the least prime divisor of m. As a check, q=2,m=3,s=3 gives counts 3,21,49 for k=1,2,3. For only c_0=0 the derivative identities give t_i=0 at any critical point. If Y_i≠0 with i≠0 then Y_{i+1}=0 and ∂_{i+1}F=c_iY_i^a≠0, a contradiction. Thus e_0 is the unique singular point. In its affine chart diagonal rescalings over the algebraic closure, starting from u_{m−1}, normalize the coefficients to the given chain. Its lowest homogeneous degree is a. The critical locus of the affine polynomial is also just the origin: the positive integer weights with degree D=a^{m−1} prime to p imply by Euler that a critical point lies on the affine hypersurface, where the derivative in the missing projective chart coordinate vanishes by ordinary Euler and Y_0=1. Hence the partials form a weighted homogeneous regular sequence in a polynomial ring. With r=m−1 and w_r=1/a, w_j=(1−w_{j+1})/a, its Hilbert-series colength ∏(1−w_j)/w_j telescopes to a^r(1−w_1)=a^r−a^{r−1}+⋯+(−1)^r. The weighted Euler identity also places f in its Jacobian ideal, giving τ=μ as algebraic colengths. This jointly verifies all permitted characteristics without a characteristic-zero topological assumption.

value.rationale: The theorem explains the difference between all-smooth behavior over the ground field and a geometrically nonempty singular boundary in a known finite-field construction. It locates that boundary, tells at exactly which extension degrees it becomes visible and how its coefficient strata are distributed, and identifies the singularity one encounters upon losing the first coefficient. This connects geometric degeneration to extension arithmetic rather than recomputing the already known count at the base field. The positive-characteristic local colength calculation makes the generic boundary fiber usable without any topological interpretation.
residual_risks: The value is a reduced-boundary and generic-degeneration description, not a solution of the scheme-theoretic discriminant or an analysis of all singular fibers.
